newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico blasts Zapatistas for pulling out of talks.
newsitem.headline: Mexico blasts Zapatistas for pulling out of talks.

text.p: Mexico's chief peace negotiators blasted Zapatista rebels on Thursday for pulling out of peace talks, accusing them of using the rise of a rival rebel force to take advantage of the government.

The Zapatista National Liberation Army (EZLN) unilaterally suspended talks with the government on Monday that had been going on intermittently since shortly after a January 1994 uprising by the rebels in the southeastern state of Chiapas.

Top government negotiator Marco Antonio Bernal on Thursday linked the pullout to the recent emergence of a new guerrilla group, the Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR), that carried out attacks in several Mexican states last week.

"We asked the EZLN not to use the presence of the EPR to try to make some kind of advantage," Bernal told a news conference. "We think...that is what the EZLN is doing, taking advantage of the presence of the EPR, and we don't think that's valid."
The sudden rise of the EPR has put pressure on the government to show progress in its peace negotiations with the Zapatistas to prevent them from taking up arms again.
The urgency, analysts say, has strengthened the hand of the Chiapas rebels to win more concessions at the bargaining table.
Bernal also accused the Zapatistas of stalling the peace process, saying, "If it's not one thing, it's another."
The Zapatistas have accused the government of negotiating in bad faith and of failing to deliver what it promised in an initial peace agreement on indigenous rights in February.
The Zapatistas demanded five conditions to renew talks, and Bernal said the government was willing to discuss all but one demand: that the government negotiators be replaced.
